newsitem.title: USA: Brent climbs in late US trade, full boats sold.
newsitem.headline: Brent climbs in late US trade, full boats sold.

text.p: Bellwether North Sea Brent climbed in late U.S. trading Wednesday with a major broker selling three full boats for March at $22.53 a barrel, traders said.
A series of partial paper March Brents changed hands at $22.45-53 a barrel. London's IPE settled at $22.46 a barrel.
February/March Brent traded at 37/38 cents, down from 44 cents at the London close, traders said.
In the U.S. Gulf Coast, foreign crudes continue to stream in on the back of the open transatlantic arbitrage.

The spread between March West Texas Intermediate/Cushing and Brent was around $1.70-80 a barrel, giving North Sea sellers ample economic incentive to bring barrels into the Gulf, even though demand there is mixed.
A ULCC of Brent for February 9-13 was recently sold at into the Gulf Coast at WTI minus 25 cents a barrel.

Talk among traders that Norwegian Oseberg would be delivered into the February NYMEX contract dissipated when it was revelaed that ARCO sold some 150,000 barrels to a U.S. refiner, averting the NYMEX delivery.
ARCO had considered the unusual move of delivering the Oseberg which it holds in its Seaway pipeline before finally selling the crude.
